source.description: Accepted CP1 node-resolution control, before the rejected list-copy experiment.

encoding: NodeId, NodeListId, AuxId, and FlowId fields retain raw owner-qualified bits. Zero denotes None only for explicitly optional fields; optional auxiliary/list/flow fields remain documentary u64 values and are not themselves owner-retention proofs.
Kinds retain the complete open i16 domain as their 16-bit unsigned representation. State records may use signed-extension encoding; compare after normalization to 16 bits.

NodeSlice stores start and len as u32. Op105 packs start in the high32 bits and len in the low32 bits, with no sentinel or truncation. Its successful relative index is below len and therefore fits u32 even though the API accepts usize.

Absent syntax lists retain a=0; descriptors with no backing retain backing=0. Allocated empty backings retain a nonzero backing ID and their exact start and zero len. Empty descriptors still take the original validation path.
All event words are obtained from existing arguments, the result of the single original read, or the already copied slice descriptor. No enrichment read or new runtime-ID assignment is performed.
limitations: Only the named successful binder helper operations are observed. These counts are not complete AST-access counts and do not measure timing, allocator cost, locks, refcounts, branch frequency outside named sites, or instruction coverage.

Only two actual kind-read sites and three actual flag-read sites in dispatch/state emit field-read records. Binder::n records successful resolutions throughout the binder, including reads that do not emit a named kind/flag record. A resolution can therefore be followed by zero or several unrecorded payload/field uses.

Op104 and op106 represent complete helper results, including descriptor validation, not each internal list/backing lookup. Op105 records the selected entry once after successful indexing. Direct indexing or iteration of a NodeSliceRead returned by syntax_nodes is not instrumented.

set_flags records a write only when the old value differs and the original setter succeeds. set_flow_node records every successful setter for a supported payload, including None and equal-value assignments; it does not claim the value changed.

Writes through binding_mut and flow_mut, node symbol/local-symbol/locals/next-container/return-flow metadata, symbol and table operations, declaration lists, direct AstView accesses, and utility or generated payload reads are excluded except for any nested Binder::n resolution events. No direct binding metadata write family beyond set_flags and set_flow_node is added.

Failed lookups, failed setters and out-of-bounds syntax indices have no success event for that operation. Earlier successful nested observations may remain before failure. The driver must reject an incomplete or failed capture; missing success records do not prove an unattempted operation.

Hooks apply to a separate copy of exact accepted CP1 source only. The observer changes generated code and stack frames; its operation sequence is diagnostic, not native CPU or allocation evidence. Parsing, pre/post state export, serialization and inactive work are excluded by recorder-controlled domain2 activation.
